thread:
Maya: Heads up — noticed a sharp jump in preemptible eviction rate in eu-west3 over the last 10m. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/cluster/eviction-heat ?view=eu-west3 :eyes:
OpsBot: [ALERT] preemptible_eviction_rate_high (eu-west3) — 7.6% over 10m — severity: P2 — paging infra-oncall
Liam: Seen it too. Is this correlated with GPU pool scale events or network flaps?
Chen: Query I used to validate: ```promql
100 * sum(rate(gcp_preemptible_evictions_total{region="eu-west3"}[10m]))
 / sum(gcp_gpu_instance_count{region="eu-west3"})
```
Chen: That gives percent-of-fleet evicted in the window. Right now shows ~7.2% if I run with 5m rate.
Sara: 7% sustained is high vs our 1% SLO for 5m tail. This could push inference tail latencies up if fallback isn't instant.
Maya: App traces show a small bump in tail lat for the realtime route (p95 from 120ms -> 180ms) coincident with evictions.
Liam: Two angles: tune alerting to reduce noise, and add a synthetic probe that exercises preemptible allocation + kv-cache warmup to measure real impact.
Chen: For alert tuning, propose a composite: evictions > 3% AND evictions_rate_increase > 3pp over 15m AND queue_latency > 100ms. Example rule: ```expr = (increase(gcp_preemptible_evictions_total{region="eu-west3"}[15m]) / max(sum(gcp_gpu_instance_count{region="eu-west3"}),1)) > 0.03 and
increase(request_queue_latency_ms_bucket{route="realtime"}[15m]) > 100
```
Sara: Agree. Also add a cooldown so we don't page for transient blips: require 2 evals (5m each).
DevOps: We should also surface hedging pool saturation. Right now hedged on-demand fallback is at 8% of capacity; ops runbook suggests 10-12% during EU morning.
Maya: What's the cost impact if we bump hedged capacity to 15% during the window? Rough calc: current spend on GPUs in eu-west3 ~ $65k/mo. 7% more on-demand -> ~ $4.5k/mo extra. We can offset by tightening batch windows elsewhere.
Liam: Can we implement dynamic hedging: increase reserved hedged when composite signal hits, and let autoscaler scale down after 30m of stability?
Chen: Technically straightforward: autoscaler policy supports a priority pool + hedged target. We need to add a short-lived override via the fleet-controller: ```yaml
- target: hedged_pool_count
  region: eu-west3
  override: +15%
  ttl: 30m
```
Sara: Also update runbook/alert flow: if composite fires, infra-oncall verifies (1) eviction trend, (2) hedged pool fill, (3) routing policies. If filled and tail still high, trigger manual fallback to reserved and notify product.
Maya: I'll add a synthetic probe to devex that launches one small job every 2m and reports allocation+warmup time. That will help separate allocation noise vs warmup-induced latency.
DevOps: Action items: Maya -> add probe (ETA: 2h); Chen -> implement composite alert + cooldown (ETA: 3h); Liam -> add autoscaler override blueprint (ETA: EOD); Sara -> update runbook and test playbook (ETA: EOD).
OpsBot: Noted tasks and assignees. Creating ticket INF-4721 and linking dashboard.
Liam: One more thought — network maintenance earlier this morning in eu-west3 might have caused transient preemptible reclaim patterns. I'll ping cloud-support for provider-side window logs.
Maya: Thanks. Will watch the probe and report back. If anyone sees paging spam from the new rule, flag me and we'll iterate. :thumbsup:
Sara: If we make the alert composite, also add a Grafana panel that shows hedged pool fill and estimated cost delta so PMs can see tradeoffs at-a-glance.
Chen: I'll add the panel and a small script to estimate cost delta from hedging percentage.
Maya: Closing loop — current status: evictions trending down to 2.1% after a region autoscaler correction, probe still warm. We'll reconvene if it creeps up again. :white_check_mark:
